speaker: alice
text: This is what happens when you actually commit to the green transition, Alex. <cite index='13-31,13-32,13-33'>Wind and solar generated 30% of EU electricity in 2025, overtaking fossil fuels at 29% for the first time, with a 19% surge in solar capacity driving the milestone whilst coal fell to a record low of 9.2%</cite>. That's not just good news, that's game-changing news.

speaker: charlie
text: And speaking of game-changers, the Goldman Environmental Prize just honoured some absolute legends this week. <cite index='11-18,11-19'>This year's recipients include Yuvelis Morales Blanco, whose tireless campaigning halted commercial fracking in Colombia, and the UK's Sarah Finch, who took big oil to court in a David versus Goliath battle and won</cite>. Ordinary people doing extraordinary things, mate.

speaker: alice
text: These are the stories that prove individual action still matters, Alex. Meanwhile, in the lab, <cite index='12-3,12-4,12-5'>evolutionary biologist Dr. Toby Kiers won the 2026 Tyler Prize for her work on mycorrhizal fungi, which act as Earth's circulatory system and draw down around 13 billion tons of CO2 each year</cite>. Nature's own carbon capture system, right under our feet!
